slides.title: Missing people is *a real signal.*
slides.sub: What an MIT study saw in the brain after a day alone.

slides.title: Ten hours alone
slides.body: MIT researchers had 40 volunteers, mostly college students, spend 10 hours alone in a windowless room with no phone. On another day, they fasted 10 hours.

slides.title: A craving response
slides.body: After isolation, photos of people together activated a midbrain area, the substantia nigra, much like food photos did after fasting.

slides.title: One honest limit
slides.body: This was one lab study: a single 10-hour stretch, mostly students. It shows a signal, not a rule about your life.

slides.title: Treat it like hunger.
slides.body: Next time you feel the pull toward people, don't scroll past it. Send one real message to someone you miss.
